content.user_title: Dispatch Independent AI Agents in Parallel
content.value_statement: Sequential debugging wastes time when failures are unrelated. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code split work into focused parallel agents.
actual_capabilities: Helps decide when failures are independent enough for parallel work.
Shows how to group failures by file, subsystem, or problem domain.
Provides a structure for focused agent prompts with scope and constraints.
Demonstrates parallel dispatch using separate agent tasks.
Defines review steps for summaries, conflicts, and full test verification.
Lists cases where parallel agents should not be used.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not launch agents by itself.
It works best when tasks have clear boundaries and little shared state.
It is not suited for exploratory debugging with an unknown root cause.
Human review is still required before accepting combined changes.

use_cases.title: Split Independent Test Failures
use_cases.description: Turn unrelated failing test files into separate agent tasks with clear expected outputs.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Refactor Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Assign separate subsystems to agents after a broad refactor creates distinct failures.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Agent Reviews
use_cases.description: Create scoped prompts and verification steps before using several AI assistants together.

prompt_templates.title: Find Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failures and tell me which ones can be handled by separate agents. Explain any shared-state risks before suggesting parallel tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Create Agent Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert known independent issues into focused assignments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one focused agent prompt for each independent problem domain. Include scope, goal, constraints, and expected summary for each agent.

prompt_templates.title: Dispatch Debugging Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: I have unrelated failures in three test areas. Build a parallel dispatch plan with one agent per area and a final integration checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Agent Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these agent summaries and proposed changes. Identify conflicts, missing verification, and the safest order to integrate the fixes.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files fail after a refactor.
output: Agent 1 investigates the abort tests and returns root cause plus changes.
Agent 2 investigates batch completion behavior and reports whether production logic changed.
Agent 3 investigates race condition tests and reports verification results.
Final review checks conflicts and runs the full suite.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether to use parallel agents for broad exploratory debugging.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a single discovery pass first, because the root cause and task boundaries are not clear yet.

output_examples.input: Two agents changed adjacent files in the same subsystem.
output_examples.output: The integration step flags possible overlap, asks for a diff review, and delays final acceptance until tests pass together.

best_practices: Group work by independent problem domain before creating agent prompts.
Give each agent a narrow scope, concrete goal, and explicit constraints.
Review summaries, check conflicts, and run the full test suite after integration.
anti_patterns: Do not dispatch parallel agents when one fix may affect all failures.
Do not ask every agent to inspect the whole codebase without boundaries.
Do not merge agent changes without reading summaries and verifying behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a decision pattern and prompt structure for environments that support agent tasks.

faq.question: When should I use one agent instead?
faq.answer: Use one agent when failures appear related, the root cause is unknown, or the work shares state.

faq.question: Can it help with non-test work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide parallel research or implementation when tasks are independent and clearly scoped.

faq.question: What should each agent receive?
faq.answer: Each agent should receive one scope, a clear goal, constraints, and the expected return summary.

faq.question: How do I avoid conflicting changes?
faq.answer: Assign separate files or subsystems, then review diffs and run shared verification before merging.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly requires summary review, conflict checks, and full verification after agents return.
